Round the compressor power to 2 decimals while tracking the level

Source: R/tank_optimization.R
tank_round_power.Rd

Rounding each slot on its own drifts the level: a third of a kW rounds to 0.33 in every slot and the tank loses 0.01 kWh of heat per slot and kW of COP. Instead each slot takes the 2-decimal power that brings the level closest to the level the unrounded solution reaches at the end of that slot, so the rounded level never strays further from it than half a rounding step of heat. The backup heater is rounded on its own and the compressor makes up its rounding; where the COP is 0 the backup heater tracks the level in the compressor's place.

Usage

tank_round_power(
  target,
  heat_demand,
  cop,
  init,
  k,
  dt,
  Pc,
  backup = 0,
  Pb = 0,
  power = NULL
)

Arguments

target

numeric vector, level at the end of each slot under the unrounded power (kWh)

heat_demand

numeric vector, heat demand (kW thermal)

cop

numeric vector, coefficient of performance

init

numeric, level before the first slot (kWh thermal)

k

numeric, per-slot retention (1 - loss/100)^dt

dt

numeric, slot length in hours

Pc

numeric, compressor cap (kW)

backup

numeric vector, backup heater power (kW, electric = thermal)

Pb

numeric, backup heater cap (kW), 0 without one

power

numeric vector, the unrounded power (kW). Where the tank ends a slot empty, the demand it leaves unserved is not for the rounding to make up: the power there stays within a rounding step of it.

Value

list of the rounded power and backup (kW)
